name: SoftSync
summary: Flexible B2B CRM for small sales teams: records and custom objects, table, pipeline and calendar views, email sync and campaigns, meeting notes and summaries, Autopilot follow-up workflows, and API and MCP access so Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini can work with the CRM directly.
best_for: small B2B sales teams of up to five people who want CRM records, email campaigns, meeting summaries and follow-up automation in one workspace, and who want Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini to work with that CRM directly rather than through a connector marketplace
skip_if: your team will pass five users soon and the jump to $59 per seat breaks the budget; you run high-volume outbound where 1,000 campaign emails per user a month is too tight; or you rely on a library of prebuilt integrations rather than an API and MCP connection
honest_knock:
Pro stops at five team members per workspace. The sixth person does not add a sixth Pro seat; it moves the whole team to Business, which is $59 per seat a month on yearly billing instead of $29. A five-person team on Pro pays $145 a month billed yearly; the same team plus one hire pays $354 on Business, for the same product surface, since the pricing page says both paid plans carry the same core features. If your team is near that line, price the Business plan now rather than after you have moved your pipeline in.

The monthly allowances are per user and per calendar month, and on Pro they are 1,000 campaign emails, 1,000 enrichments and 1,000 AI chats, with one connected mailbox per user. A single rep running cold outreach from SoftSync can reach 1,000 campaign emails well before the month ends, and the page does not say what happens when you do, whether sending stops or an overage is charged. Ask before you plan a campaign around it.

Month-to-month billing costs about a third more than yearly: $39 against $29 on Pro, $79 against $59 on Business. There is no free plan, and the pricing page does not state a trial length; it says the checkout shows any trial terms. SoftSync's own home page says it has no integrations directory and instead gives your AI agent a way in through the API and MCP access; if your stack depends on ready-made connectors, check the specific ones on the integrations page before you commit. We found no independent buyer reviews we could read, so the only voices on the site are the testimonials SoftSync chose, most of them from founders and investors rather than daily users.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-26 on softsync.ai/pricing in a headless browser, including the plan table and every pricing FAQ answer) Two standard paid plans, priced per seat per month, plus a custom Enterprise tier; there is no free plan. Pro is $29 per seat a month billed yearly or $39 billed monthly, and Business is $59 per seat a month billed yearly or $79 monthly; the page says yearly billing saves about 25%, and its FAQ says prices exclude VAT. Enterprise is custom-priced. Both paid plans carry the same feature set: flexible records and custom objects, table, pipeline and calendar views, email sync, campaigns and templates, meeting notes and summaries, a desktop recorder and Chrome extension, reports and dashboards, the AI Assistant, Autopilot workflows, record and contact enrichment, integrations, API and MCP access. What changes is capacity: Pro allows at most 5 team members and 10 groups per workspace, 250,000 records per table and 1 mailbox connection per user, with 1,000 campaign emails, 1,000 enrichments and 1,000 chats per user per calendar month; Business raises those to 25 team members, 100 groups, 1,000,000 records, 5 mailboxes and 10,000 of each monthly allowance, and adds Priority Support for data migration and a workspace consultant, which are self-served on Pro. The page also lists prices in EUR, GBP, AUD, CAD, NZD, CHF, DKK, SEK, NOK and ISK. It publishes no trial length: the FAQ says the checkout page shows any trial terms and whether payment details are needed. Early-stage teams can ask about startup pricing on a call.

compare_with.name: folk
compare_with.why: folk is the closest comparison in our own dossiers: also a lightweight, per-seat CRM for small teams that dislike heavyweight sales software. On folk's published prices (re-verified 3 September 2026) Standard is $24 per member a month billed yearly or $30 monthly, against SoftSync Pro at $29 or $39, so folk is the cheaper entry by $5 to $9 a seat. folk also states its trial openly, two weeks without a credit card, where SoftSync's pricing page leaves it to the checkout. SoftSync puts more of the sales day inside the one plan: email campaigns, meeting notes and summaries, a desktop recorder, Autopilot workflows and MCP access for AI assistants are all on Pro, and its enrichment allowance is 1,000 per user a month against folk's 500 on Standard. folk has no five-person ceiling on its entry plan. A team that mainly manages relationships and contacts fits folk; a team of five or fewer that wants outreach, meetings and automation in one place, and wants an AI assistant to act on the records, fits SoftSync.

vendor_mcp.what: Server at api.softsync.ai/mcp/softsync that reads and writes your CRM: create, query, bulk-update and merge records, find duplicates, search messages, write notes, send templated emails or whole campaigns, and run published workflows.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their FAQ: "AI, MCP, and API access are included on every plan." Every plan is paid — from $29 per seat a month billed yearly — after a 14-day trial.
